source: NCERT Class XI, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 1), Ch. 7 (Indian Bronze Sculpture).

sections.heading: 1. The Lost-Wax Technique
points: Indian bronzes were cast by the **lost-wax (cire perdue) process**: a wax model is coated in clay, the wax melted out, and molten metal poured in.
The tradition goes back to the **Indus Valley (Dancing Girl)** and continued for over 4000 years.
Bronze images were made for **worship, rituals and processions** (Buddhist, Jain and Hindu).

sections.heading: 2. Early and Medieval Bronzes
points: **Buddhist bronzes** — from sites like **Amaravati, Nalanda** (Pala period, Bihar/Bengal) and **Nagapattinam (TN)**.
**Jain bronzes** — from **Chausa (Bihar)**, Akota (Gujarat).
**Himachal and Kashmir** produced fine bronzes too.

sections.heading: 3. Chola Bronzes — The Pinnacle
points: The **Chola period (9th–13th c., Tamil Nadu)** produced the **finest Indian bronzes**.

The most celebrated is the **Nataraja** — **Shiva as the Lord of Dance** in the **ananda tandava** pose, within a ring of flames (prabhamandala), holding the damaru (drum) and agni (fire), standing on the dwarf **Apasmara**.
Chola bronzes are noted for **grace, balance, and lifelike modelling**; the queen **Sembiyan Mahadevi** was a great patron.
Portable bronzes were carried in temple processions.

sections.heading: 4. Significance and Symbolism
points: The **Nataraja** symbolises the cosmic cycle of **creation and destruction** and the rhythm of the universe.
Bronzes reflect deep religious devotion and mastery of metallurgy.
Later Vijayanagara and Nayaka periods continued the bronze tradition.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Indian bronzes = lost-wax (cire perdue) technique; from Indus Dancing Girl onward.
Chola bronzes (Tamil Nadu) = the finest; Nataraja (Shiva Lord of Dance) is the masterpiece.
Nataraja: ananda tandava pose, ring of flames, damaru + agni, dwarf Apasmara underfoot.
Pala bronzes = Nalanda (Bihar/Bengal); Jain bronzes = Chausa, Akota.
Sembiyan Mahadevi = great Chola patron of bronzes.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Indian bronzes use the **lost-wax (cire perdue)** technique.
The **Nataraja** (Shiva as Lord of Dance) is the finest **Chola** bronze.
The dwarf under Nataraja's foot is **Apasmara** (ignorance).
The **Pala** bronzes come from **Nalanda** (eastern India).
